newsitem.title: DENMARK: Strong crown boosts Danish bond prices.
newsitem.headline: Strong crown boosts Danish bond prices.

text.p: Danish bond prices opened up on Tuesday, with the strong crown helping to narrow the Danish-German benchmark yield gap.

At 0715 GMT the crown traded at 3.8067 to the mark, its highest level against the German currency since early 1993. The 10-year yield gap with Germany edged in to 68 basis points, from Monday's 69 and dealers saw it staying around that level.
"It looks as though the yield gap could hold at below 70 basis points," a dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 rose 0.16 point to 109.34.
Dealers saw it trading in a range of 109.20 to 109.60, at least until the publication of U.S. employment cost data at 1230 GMT. --Stig Pedersen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969659
